questions.q: Which bank statement format is the most common standard for US bank statements?
questions.explain: BAI2 (Bank Administration Institute, version 2) is a plain-text, line-based format that originated in the US and remains the most common US statement format.

questions.q: In a BAI2 file, what does a '16' record type represent?
questions.explain: Record type 16 is the transaction detail line — one per transaction, each carrying a BAI2 transaction type code.

questions.q: In an MT940 message, what does the :61: tag represent?
options: A statement line, one per transaction
questions.explain: The :61: tag is the statement line, with one appearing per transaction, often followed by an :86: tag with narrative detail.

questions.q: What kind of file structure does CAMT.053 use, compared to BAI2 and MT940?
options: A flat, line-based structure identical to BAI2
Structured XML, part of the ISO 20022 messaging family
questions.explain: CAMT.053 is structured XML under the ISO 20022 standard, more verbose but more explicit than BAI2 or MT940's flat line formats.

questions.q: Why might a single multinational company receive bank statements in more than one of these formats?
options: Oracle requires a different format for each legal entity
Different banks, or the same bank in different countries, may send different formats, and Oracle loads all of them into the same internal structure
Only CAMT.053 is supported outside the US
Companies must manually convert every format to BAI2 before loading
questions.explain: Different banks and countries commonly use different formats; Oracle Fusion Cash Management supports all of them and normalizes them into the same internal statement structure.
